A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UDS research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original fine-tuning accuracy and throughput results in Table 3, with additional ablations and robustness experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical results and adds a within-batch diversity ablation in Appendix C.7 and Table 16.

M1.justification: Equation 9 introduces an optional within-batch distance term, evaluated as a scoring variant in Appendix C.7. Default UDS explicitly omits this addition and retains the same nuclear-norm scoring, projection, FIFO buffer, and top-K selection.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, ScienceQA, GSM8K, CodeAlpaca/HumanEval, MATH, and GSM8K-to-MATH500/AMC23 generalization. V3's expanded dataset descriptions document existing coverage; its new ablation uses retained benchmarks.

E2.justification: Regular, Random, MaxLoss, MaxGrad, RHO-Loss, GREATS, and FisherSFT remain in their corresponding comparisons. The added Table 16 tests an internal UDS variant; no baseline method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Existing splits, backbones, selection fractions, training budgets, batch sizes, and metrics are retained. Appendix C.7 explicitly follows Table 3's experimental settings for the new scoring ablation. Newly listed dataset sizes are disclosures, not reported setting changes.

E4.justification: Appendix C.7 adds a targeted ablation testing whether within-batch diversity improves on historical-buffer diversity. Existing component, hyperparameter, projection, buffer-policy, long-context, and OOD analyses remain. The Frobenius-norm correlation analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four repetitions with different random seeds and retain the same uncertainty reporting and correlation/p-value plots. Table 16 follows the existing reporting practice without announcing additional runs or a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 16 newly reports within-batch-variant scores of 63.28, 95.26, 79.80, and 46.39% on MMLU, ScienceQA, GSM8K, and HumanEval, respectively, finding no notable accuracy difference. Matched pre-existing numerical results and plotted data are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 9 extends the mathematical definition of the diversity score with an optional within-batch term. Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, the optimization derivations, and the proofs in v2 Appendix C/v3 Appendix D otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: joint utility/diversity selection without external resources, superior benchmark performance, and greater training efficiency.

C2.justification: New Appendix B discusses prior offline filtering of noisy data and interprets selection as implicit curriculum learning. Section 3.2 and Appendix C.7 explain omitting within-batch diversity, although C.7 reverses the main text's buffer/batch relationship. Existing SVD-cost and theoretical-proof limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 expands dataset documentation and consolidates train/test mappings. Table 17 newly lists MATH's 7,500/5,000 training/test samples, MATH500's 500 test samples, and AMC23's 40 test samples for existing experiments. Training hyperparameters and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V3 credits Cui et al. (2020) for nuclear-norm inspiration and adds Xie et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2021). Appendix B expands positioning relative to offline selection, curriculum learning, and active learning. Ren et al. (2021) and Loquercio et al. (2020) are removed with the corresponding future-work suggestion.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose and pseudocode revisions, adds a Discussions appendix, an Impact Statement, and a brief Hyperparameter Analysis subsection, and removes the LLM Usage Declaration. Most existing prose and the scientific section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout with extensive reflow. Figure 1 is redrawn; old Figures 2, 3, and 9 become panels of Figure 2; the memory-sensitivity plot moves into the main text. V3 also adds Table 16 and expands the dataset table.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful evidence for omitting within-batch diversity, fills dataset-documentation gaps, and improves attribution and explanation. These gains are limited because the core results and proofs are retained. The reversed buffer/batch explanation in Appendix C.7 introduces a small inconsistency, but does not outweigh the targeted improvements.
